meta.note: Course names, durations, specializations, and tuition fees in the 'faculties' section are real data provided by the project owner. All other sections (fee breakdown formula, eligibility, semester structure, timings, exam pattern, attendance policy, syllabus structure, lateral entry, add-on certifications) are generated for this academic project to be realistic and internally consistent with Parul University's actual scale (50,000+ students, 25+ faculties, multi-campus infrastructure). These generated sections should not be treated as officially confirmed university policy.

data_types.verified_by_user: Real data provided directly by the project owner
data_types.generated_for_project: Realistic, scale-consistent data created for this academic project

semester_and_credit_system.structure: Two semesters per academic year — Odd Semester (July to December) and Even Semester (January to June).
semester_and_credit_system.credit_system: Choice Based Credit System (CBCS). Undergraduate engineering programs typically carry 20-24 credits per semester; management, commerce, and liberal arts programs typically carry 18-22 credits per semester; postgraduate programs typically carry 16-20 credits per semester.
semester_and_credit_system.grading_scale: 10-point CGPA scale. Grade bands: O (Outstanding, 90-100%), A+ (80-89%), A (70-79%), B+ (60-69%), B (55-59%), C (50-54%), P (Pass, 40-49%), F (Fail, below 40%).
semester_and_credit_system.cgpa_to_percentage: Approximate conversion: Percentage = (CGPA - 0.5) x 10, though official conversion certificates are issued by the examination department on request.

class_timing.campus_hours: 9:30 AM to 4:20 PM, Monday to Saturday (as per general campus timing).
class_timing.lecture_duration: Each lecture period is typically 50-55 minutes.
class_timing.lab_sessions: Laboratory and practical sessions are held in 2-3 hour blocks, typically 2-3 times per week depending on the course and semester.
class_timing.weekly_pattern: A typical week includes 20-26 contact hours combining lectures, tutorials, and lab/practical sessions, varying by faculty and program type.
class_timing.weekly_off: Sundays are a general holiday; some faculties (e.g. Medicine, Nursing) may have rotational duty schedules including weekends for clinical postings.

exam_pattern.internal_assessment: Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA) typically contributes 30-40% of the total grade, based on mid-semester tests, assignments, quizzes, and attendance/participation.
exam_pattern.end_semester_exam: The End-Semester Examination typically contributes 60-70% of the total grade, held at the end of each semester.
exam_pattern.exam_months: Odd semester exams are typically held in November-December; even semester exams are typically held in April-May.
exam_pattern.backlog_policy: Students who do not clear a subject may reappear in the subsequent semester's supplementary/backlog examination, typically scheduled 4-8 weeks after result declaration. A fee per backlog subject applies.
exam_pattern.revaluation: Students may apply for photocopy of answer sheets and/or revaluation within a specified window (typically 10-15 days) after result declaration, subject to a per-subject fee.

attendance_policy.minimum_required: A minimum of 75% attendance per subject per semester is required to be eligible to sit for the end-semester examination, in line with standard AICTE/UGC norms followed by most Indian universities.
attendance_policy.condonation: Students with attendance between 65% and 74% may apply for condonation with valid supporting documentation (medical certificate, family emergency, university-representation in sports/cultural events), subject to approval by the Head of Department/Dean.
attendance_policy.detention: Students with attendance below 65% (without an approved condonation) are typically detained from appearing in that subject's end-semester exam and may need to repeat the semester/subject.

general_academic_policies.medium_of_instruction: English is the primary medium of instruction across all faculties. Reference material in regional languages (Hindi/Gujarati) may be available for select subjects in Law, Ayurveda, and Homeopathy programs, but examinations and core instruction remain in English.

lateral_entry_and_credit_transfer.diploma_to_btech: Diploma Engineering holders are eligible for lateral entry directly into the 2nd year of the corresponding B.Tech program, subject to seat availability and meeting minimum diploma marks criteria.
lateral_entry_and_credit_transfer.bsc_to_btech: B.Sc. graduates in relevant subjects may be eligible for lateral entry into select B.Tech/B.Sc. programs with second-year standing, subject to department approval and bridge-course completion if required.
lateral_entry_and_credit_transfer.credit_transfer_from_other_universities: Students transferring from other UGC-recognized universities may receive credit transfer for equivalent completed subjects, subject to syllabus comparison and approval by the respective faculty's academic committee.
lateral_entry_and_credit_transfer.general_note: All lateral entry and credit transfer decisions are made on a case-by-case basis by the respective faculty and are subject to AICTE/UGC regulations in effect for that academic year.

addon_certification_programs.description: In addition to the core curriculum, the university offers optional industry-aligned certification programs to enhance student employability, generally available to students from Semester 4 onward.
certifications_available: AWS Cloud Practitioner / AWS Solutions Architect (Amazon Web Services)
Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals / Power Platform
addon_certification_programs.eligibility_note: Availability and eligibility for specific certifications vary by faculty and may carry a separate nominal fee and minimum academic cutoff (commonly referenced in university communications as part of a broader Global Certification Forum initiative).

syllabus_structure_pattern.description: While detailed subject-wise syllabi differ by course and are maintained by individual departments, most undergraduate programs at Parul University generally follow this year-wise structure:
syllabus_structure_pattern.year_1: Foundational subjects common across the faculty (basic sciences, communication skills, introduction to the discipline, environmental studies).
syllabus_structure_pattern.year_2: Core discipline subjects begin, along with foundational labs/practicals specific to the specialization.
syllabus_structure_pattern.year_3: Specialization-focused core and elective subjects, increased lab/practical/project component, and (for eligible programs) internship exposure.
syllabus_structure_pattern.final_year: Advanced electives, major project/dissertation, industry internship, and placement preparation activities run in parallel with academics.
syllabus_structure_pattern.postgraduate_note: Postgraduate (PG) programs generally follow a condensed 2-year version of this structure: Year 1 covers core/advanced subjects, Year 2 focuses on specialization electives, a research project/dissertation, and (for professional PG programs like MBA) a mandatory internship.

eligibility_by_faculty.note: Eligibility is grouped by faculty since it is realistically consistent across a faculty's undergraduate offerings. Specific minimum percentages may vary slightly by category (General/Reserved) and are subject to change per admission cycle — always confirm current-year criteria with the admissions office.

Faculty of Engineering and Technology.pg_eligibility: Relevant B.Tech/B.E. degree with minimum 50% aggregate (45% for reserved categories). GATE score preferred but not always mandatory.

Faculty of Management Studies.pg_eligibility: Graduation in any discipline with minimum 50% aggregate. CAT/MAT/CMAT/university entrance test scores considered for MBA.

Faculty of Commerce.ug_eligibility: 10+2 in any stream (Commerce background preferred), minimum 45% aggregate.

Faculty of Fine Arts.ug_eligibility: 10+2 in any stream, minimum 45% aggregate, plus a portfolio/practical demonstration.

Faculty of Liberal Arts.pg_eligibility: Graduation in a relevant subject with minimum 50% aggregate.

fee_structure_formula.description: Beyond the base tuition fee (which is real, per-course data provided by the university), most Indian private universities charge several additional standardized fee components. The formula below is a realistic generated estimate for this project, expressed as a percentage/fixed addition to the real tuition fee, rather than a fabricated absolute number for each of the 150+ individual specializations.

components.tuition_fee: As listed per course/specialization in the 'faculties' section below — this is real, verified data.
components.development_fee: Approximately 8-10% of the annual tuition fee, covering infrastructure and campus development.
components.examination_fee: ₹3,000 to ₹5,000 per year for undergraduate programs; ₹4,000 to ₹6,000 per year for postgraduate/doctoral programs.
components.other_charges: ₹2,000 to ₹3,500 per year, covering ID card, library access, sports facilities, and student welfare activities.
components.one_time_admission_fee: ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, charged only in the first year at the time of admission.
components.refundable_caution_deposit: ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, refundable at the time of course completion or withdrawal, subject to no pending dues.
